title: Trump Hails Indian-Origin Astronaut Anil Menon as 'Great Patriot' During ISS Call
excerpt: President calls Menon, Jessica Meir, and Jack Hathaway 'brave people' and invites them to the Oval Office; announces new US Space Academy.
body:
• President Trump praised Indian-origin NASA astronaut Anil Menon and crewmates Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway as "great Americans, great patriots, brave people" during a live call to the International Space Station on August 29.
  • Trump invited the crew to the Oval Office upon their return and announced plans for a US Space Academy to be placed at the level of West Point and the Naval Academy.
  • Menon, a colonel in the US Space Force, described completing a spacewalk the previous week and expressed pride in preparations for Moon and Mars missions.
  • Born in Minneapolis to Indian and Ukrainian immigrant parents, Menon is a Harvard-educated emergency medicine physician who served as SpaceX's first flight surgeon before joining NASA's astronaut corps.

The Call From Houston

President Donald Trump called the International Space Station on Friday from NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, speaking with the three American astronauts aboard the orbital laboratory.

"This is a great honor, to be with you is a great honor and I just want to thank Jessica, Anil, Jack, great Americans, great patriots, brave people," Trump told astronauts Anil Menon, Jessica Meir, and Jack Hathaway, who are serving as part of Expedition 75.

Trump praised their courage, noting that even being selected for the mission was an achievement in itself. He was characteristically candid: "I wouldn't do it. I will tell you right now, I hate to admit it, I would not want to do it, but some people love it more than anything."

He invited the crew to visit the Oval Office after their return. "We're going to see you when you get back. In fact, if you want, Oval Office time, right?"

Menon Speaks From Orbit

Colonel Anil Menon, who serves in the US Space Force, responded with evident pride. "Thank you, sir. And I would like to say, as a colonel in the Space Force, that I am very proud to serve in the largest domain imaginable," he said.

Menon described a spacewalk he had completed the previous week, saying he viewed the space station from the robotic arm and witnessed "the incredible ingenuity that we are capable of." He has completed three spacewalks totaling over 19 hours during the mission so far.

"We are going to pave the way to our next journey to the Moon, Moon Base and Mars. And thank you for propelling us in that direction."

— Anil Menon, NASA Astronaut and US Space Force Colonel

Menon's wife, Anna Menon — herself a NASA astronaut who flew to space on SpaceX's Polaris Dawn mission in September 2024 — joined Trump at the space center. "Hi, it's Anna. Great to see you guys up there. We love you guys. You're doing a great job," she told the crew.

From Minneapolis to Orbit

Anil Menon, 49, was born and raised in Minneapolis to parents who immigrated from India and Ukraine. His father, Shankaran Menon, is originally from Kerala. Menon graduated from Harvard University with a degree in neurobiology and earned a medical degree and master's in mechanical engineering from Stanford University.

His career before space was already extraordinary. As a US Air Force flight surgeon, he deployed to Afghanistan during Operation Enduring Freedom and logged over 100 sorties in the F-15. He worked with the Himalayan Rescue Association providing emergency care to climbers on Mount Everest, responded to the 2010 Haiti earthquake and the 2015 Nepal earthquake, and spent a year in India as a Rotary Ambassadorial Scholar supporting polio immunization programs.

He joined NASA in 2014 as a flight surgeon before moving to SpaceX in 2018, where he became the company's first flight surgeon and helped launch its first crewed mission, Demo-2. NASA selected him for its astronaut corps in December 2021.

A New Space Academy

The call followed Trump's announcement of plans for a US Space Academy, which he signed via executive order at the Johnson Space Center. The proposed institution would train the next generation of civilian and military aerospace professionals and be placed at the same level as West Point, the Naval Academy, the Coast Guard Academy, and the Air Force Academy.

"If we're going to do it, it has to be at that very high level. Those are among the hardest schools to get into in the whole country," Trump said. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will chair the Presidential Commission on the Space Academy, with Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson serving as executive director.

Trump also expressed pride in establishing the Space Force during his first term, arguing that space-based intelligence has become crucial to US military operations.

What's Next

Menon launched to the ISS on July 14 aboard the Roscosmos Soyuz MS-29 spacecraft alongside cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina. He is expected to remain aboard the station for an eight-month mission conducting research on how microgravity affects blood flow, vein structure, and blood composition — work aimed at preparing for future long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars.
nri_angle: An Indian-American astronaut from an immigrant family receives presidential recognition, embodying the diaspora's contributions to America's most ambitious scientific endeavors.
